headline: Social media users are joking that AI-lab staff should treat any romantic interest as a possible spy after a report on OpenAI's security advice.
score_reason: Light viral story with a real security backdrop; pool score kept.
importance_line: It shows how worry about spying at AI labs, after an FBI case, has spilled into public humour, but the security guidance itself comes from a Wall Street Journal report.
summary: Business Insider reports that jokes spread on X after the Wall Street Journal wrote about security guidance for AI-lab staff, including a post by WSJ reporter Erin Woo saying OpenAI tells employees to ask whether someone seducing them could be a spy. The jokes follow the FBI's arrest of OpenAI employee Abdulrahman Alfozan, charged with bugging a conference room, and drew replies from figures including Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer.
notes: WSJ original not read; Business Insider relays it.
